content:
Hi, I've recently been working with new and moderately experienced Lean users, and nearly every single one of them is confused about how lake works, and they often end up waiting several hours for mathlib to compile or in orange bar hell. I'm trying to collect a list of things that people find confusing about lake. I unfortunately don't have solutions for many of these but I thought I would post them anyways in the hopes that some of them can get resolved.

  • Cache problems
    • The cache often fails to download, but they don't run lake exe cache get or the VSCode action for downloading the cache. This is the most common problem in my experience. There's supposed to be some kind of behavior which downloads the cache automatically and sometimes I see it happening but it fails to run a lot of the time. Usually they encounter this issue the first time they import Mathlib, so it could be that lake build succeeds but their computer still hangs for a while.
    • lake exe cache get often hangs for a long time on Windows. Sometimes I cancel lake exe cache get after it runs for 2 minutes without printing anything to the console because I think it got stuck, but then I run it again and after 3 minutes then it starts printing things and downloading stuff.
    • There's no indicator for whether or not the cache has been downloaded already. If you aren't looking too closely at which files are being compiled, you might think that the cache has not yet been downloaded but in reality it is just building the project.
  • Compilation problems
    • Users expect lake build to compile their entire project, but they also forget to add everything to their top level file (i.e. the equivalent of Mathlib.lean) so lake build succeeds very quickly, but then they go into a particular file and it fails to typecheck. This also leads to green check marks from GitHub actions when the project is failing to compile.
    • Importing mathlib seems to take about 3 minutes on Windows. (I personally run Lean within WSL on my Windows computer because of this.) This is not a lake problem, but people often confuse a long loading time with Lean being stuck indefinitely due to a lake issue.
    • The message Imports are out of date and should be rebuilt; use the "Restart File" command in your editor. is confusing to new users. I think we should explicitly tell them that this message often appears if they have either modified an upstream file or updated a library.
    • They are still allowed to work on files where they get an Imports are out of date message, and often don't notice the message. This leads to surprises when the new constants they add to the upstream file are not reflected in the downstream file.
  • Creating new projects
    • Mathlib is not available in the default result of lake new, requiring them to add it explicitly. Maybe it would be better to force users to pick an option from std, exe, lib, math-lax, and math explicitly, and prompt them with a menu if they don't.
    • If you create a new project with lake new, it lacks a lake-manifest.json, but this will be created the next time lake is run. and then add a mathlib dependency, then lake build will fail with the message error: missing manifest; use `lake update` to generate one. But this is a misleading message because the same message happens even when there is in fact a lake-manifest, and it's just out of date.
  • Updates and dependencies
    • Users run lake update thinking that it might fix things with their installation, but don't realize that it is actually a "destructive" command that modifies the lake manifest and forces them to redownload the cache. This is not helped by the fact that if you just updated the lakefile.toml, it actually tells you to run lake update without explaining that it is destructive.
    • As far as I can tell, there's no way to add a dependency without bumping all dependencies & lean to their latest version. If I add something to lakefile.toml, then lake is completely broken for me until I run lake update.
    • I recently had an issue where I ran lake update and it said
info: leanprover-community/mathlib: checking out revision '9b51fe6ec0377d1e0f1ebeb551a7ab8d9ad8f3a4'
info: doc-gen4: checking out revision '799154a6ee3cefd3c0c89a68a81911fb83b7755c'
info: updating toolchain to 'leanprover/lean4:v4.30.0-rc2'
info: restarting Lake via Elan
error: failed to parse latest release tag

and it didn't download the newest lean version until I ran lean --version. This left me with a situation where the lean-toolchain file was updated but lake-manifest.json was not updated. Then when I ran lake build it failed with a bunch of errors like

error: Batteries/Classes/Cast.lean:12:0: Invalid definition `LibraryNote.coercion_into_rings`, may not access declaration `Batteries.Util.instInhabitedLibraryNote` marked as `meta`
error: Lean exited with code 1

presumably because the Lean version bumped but the packages didn't. I think you can trigger the second error by manually updating lean-toolchain. lake is going to have bugs and that's okay, but I think it should also do some sanity checks to make sure all the versions are compatible with each other and give the user a more helpful error message.

Niels Voss said:

  • Cache problems

It looks like you're talking about lake exe cache and not lake cache. This is in Mathlib and unrelated to lake. There's a new lake cache coming, which is implemented differently so maybe it'll solve the issues you described. (I don't know how to use it, but maybe after mathlib4-nightly-testing#203 is merged Mathlib contributors will get their hands on it)

I had heard several months ago that lake cache was being developed but I didn't realize it was so far along already. Hopefully it fixes some of the issues, and also allows caches for non-mathlib projects.
Something that would be really useful would be for the Restart file button in the infoview to tell you how many files need rebuilding, so that you know whether the number is big or amall

Yaël Dillies said:

Filed as vscode-lean4#771
But how is vscode-lean4 supposed to accomplish this? This should be a core RFC, unrelated to the VSCode extension
Currently even lake build itself doesn't seem to know how many files need to be rebuilt, so asking this from the VSCode extension seems farfetched.
You are correct @Snir Broshi ; the linked issue is just for the UI feature, but it is blocked on being able to retrieve this data from Lake.

Niels Voss said:

  • As far as I can tell, there's no way to add a dependency without bumping all dependencies & lean to their latest version. If I add something to lakefile.toml, then lake is completely broken for me until I run lake update.

The rule-of-thumb I'm using quite happily is that whenever you think you should call lake update, call lake -R clean first. It's less destructive and either works or, in this case, it tells you the solution to the riddle:

**error:** dependency 'importGraph' not in manifest; use `lake update importGraph` to add it
These sorts of clever tricks are hopeless for beginners though.
